title: Wendell and the Oath
premise: Beatrix Ashgrove has spent her life in the Ashen Valley, the one place where magic cannot follow, serving as a royal food-taster whose body is slowly poisoned into immunity. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands, she learns King Aldric is bound to an ancient entity wearing his crown — and that the map is the only key to unbinding him. Pursued by the crown's hunters and guided by Wendell, a disgraced oath-keeper who once failed to save the last king, Beatrix must choose between the valley that kept her safe and a kingdom that would use her up. In the end she breaks the binding not with the map's magic but by taking the oath herself, trading her immunity and her return home for Aldric's freedom — and discovering that inheritance is not what we are given, but what we refuse to pass on.
about_author: Theo Almeida is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six years tasting other people's recipes before writing about someone who tastes them for survival. They live near a river valley and remain suspicious of anything served without explanation.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She swallows poison for the crown at a banquet, cataloguing flavors like prayers, while establishing the Ashen Valley's magicless safety and her mother's warning never to leave. Emotional beat: quiet resignation — she believes survival is a life's whole work.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Millrace
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A bleeding courier collapses at the mill where she buys flour, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'the crown eats him' before dying. Valley wardens arrive too late. Emotional beat: fear and unwanted responsibility as the map burns cold against her skin.

chapters.title: What Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The warden-captain demands the map; when Beatrix hesitates, he reveals the valley's elders have always known about the king's binding — and chose silence. She flees toward the valley's edge. Emotional beat: betrayal of home, first act of defiance.

chapters.title: Wendell of the Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Waiting beyond the border stones, Wendell recognizes the map's seal — he drew it, twenty years ago, for a king he failed to save. He intercepts Beatrix intending to take it from her. Emotional beat: shame sharpened into pragmatism.

chapters.title: Two Liars on a Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Neither trusts the other: Beatrix hides her taster's training, Wendell hides that the map requires an oath-bound bearer. They survive an ambush by crown hunters using her poison-callused senses. Emotional beat: grudging respect kindled in danger.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They reach Corvane, the capital, where the entity's influence shows in silver-eyed officials and food that tastes of ash to her trained tongue alone. Emotional beat: horror — her curse is suddenly the kingdom's only instrument of truth.

chapters.title: An Audience of Ash
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Posing as a new court taster, she meets King Aldric and tastes the binding itself: something ancient, patient, feeding. He begs her with his eyes while his mouth praises the soup. Emotional beat: compassion for a prisoner no one sees.

chapters.title: The Oath-Keeper's Confession
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He tells Beatrix the truth: the map leads to the First Hearth, where oaths are forged, and only a willing bearer can unbind a king — the last bearer died because he refused. Emotional beat: grief finally spoken aloud after twenty years.

chapters.title: Silver Eyes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The entity, calling itself the Regent, summons Beatrix privately — it knows what she carries. It offers her wealth, safety, her old life back. Emotional beat: temptation made intimate; she realizes it fears her tongue more than any army.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Undercity
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Refusing the Regent, she flees through Corvane's tunnels with Wendell, betrayed by a servant girl she'd trusted. Wendell takes a blade meant for her. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness entangled — she cannot tell duty from love anymore.

chapters.title: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Recovering in a smuggler's caravan, Wendell watches Beatrix ration their food with a taster's precision and realizes she has been quietly poisoning herself against the Regent's agents all along. Emotional beat: awe — she has been fighting since chapter one.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They shelter in a town erased from records by the Regent generations ago; its people remember nothing, not even their children's names. Emotional beat: dread — this is the future of every place the crown-eater finishes.

chapters.title: What My Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A letter hidden in the map's lining reveals her mother was a former oath-bearer who fled to the valley pregnant, choosing Beatrix's safety over the kingdom. Emotional beat: fury and forgiveness colliding; inheritance reframed as choice.

chapters.title: Hunters on the White Pass
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Regent's elite hunters corner them on the mountain pass. Beatrix identifies a poison in the snowmelt and turns the hunters' own weapons against them; Wendell nearly dies holding the line. Emotional beat: they stop pretending this is duty.

chapters.title: The First Hearth
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They reach the ruined forge where oaths were first bound, and the map resolves into instructions: a king can be unbound only if another willingly takes the oath in his place. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — there was never a way out that didn't cost a self.

chapters.title: Wendell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell attempts to take the oath himself, to redeem his failure, but the Hearth rejects him — broken oaths cannot hold new ones. Only an unsworn, unbound person qualifies. Emotional beat: despair; he realizes Beatrix is the only candidate left.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She descends toward Corvane to face the Regent, writing letters she may never send — one to her mother, one to Wendell, one to the valley. Emotional beat: calm acceptance hardening into resolve; she chooses, and choosing frees her.

chapters.title: The Crown Eats
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the throne room, the Regent offers its final bargain: Aldric's life for her compliance. Beatrix stalls, tasting every air current, every cup, buying seconds while Wendell breaches the vault beneath the hall. Emotional beat: terror wielded like a tool.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the climax, she speaks the oath from the First Hearth and takes the binding into herself as Wendell shatters the crown-anchor below. The Regent unravels screaming; Aldric collapses free, human, weeping. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled — the price paid in full.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Beatrix survives, but the oath has burned away her immunity and left the binding's echo in her blood; she can taste magic now, everywhere, and it never stops. Aldric offers her anything. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory — saved, but changed past returning.

chapters.title: The Border Stones
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She travels home to the valley's edge and finds she cannot cross — the oath binds her to the kingdom she saved. Her mother meets her at the stones, and they grieve and laugh together. Emotional beat: mourning the old life without regret.

chapters.title: A New Oath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later, Beatrix trains a new generation of tasters and oath-bearers under Aldric's reformed crown, with Wendell beside her teaching what broken oaths teach best. She plants a garden at the border stones. Emotional beat: inheritance completed — she passes on what she refused to let die.
